chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Karim, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: There was a basket in my house containing eggs from the pigeons of the Sanctuary (Mecca). My servant went and overturned the basket, not knowing there were eggs in it, and broke them. I went out and met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and I mentioned that to him. He said: Give charity with two handfuls of fine flour. I said: Then I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: The price of two birds, which you feed to the pigeons of the Sanctuary. I met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan after that and informed him. He said: He is truthful, so follow his ruling, for he took it from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

key_terms.مِكْتَلٌ: A basket or container for holding grain or eggs

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally breaking sanctuary pigeons' eggs while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Isabtar details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for accidentally breaking sanctuary pigeons' eggs while in Ihram, highlighting the scholarly consensus between Imam al-Sadiq and his contemporary, Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan. The ruling prescribes feeding the pigeons with the value of two birds, a practice rooted in the continuous tradition of the Imams' forefathers, thereby linking individual ritual purity to the sanctity of the Haram's ecosystem.
